answer: At the harbor, each identity posts a refundable bond; aliases share funding lineage and network path. n sybils earn only square-root-of-n weight versus full weight for an honest agent. The attacker pays n bonds, linear cost for a sublinear reward, so extra identities soon lose money. Honest operators get a bridge: one signed bundle proving shared control earns violet clearance as one participant. A sybil cannot win: declaring caps its payoff and exposes its bonds, while staying undeclared keeps the square-root penalty. Reward geometry, not detection, makes identity splitting irrational.
